lines.text: Turning uses the same maths. Distance becomes angle; speed becomes omega, the spin rate.
The heading error stays between minus pi and pi radians, so it turns the short way.
Top spin: six radians per second, almost a turn a second. Spin braking, alpha: six radians per second squared.
Stopping from top spin: omega squared over two alpha. Three radians, about one hundred seventy-two degrees.
Braking early at top spin: zero point zero five seconds is zero point three radians.
The gentle line, five times the angle, meets the curve at zero point four eight radians, about twenty-seven degrees.
Inside zero point three degrees, the spin command is zero.
For a ninety degree turn: curve four point three four, line seven point eight five, cap six.
Smallest: four point three four radians per second. It shows up again in the code.
And the margin rule: plan six, below the limiter's eight.
